message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 atm) water freezes at roughly **–2 °C**.

**Why?**  
The melting/freezing point of water drops as the external pressure falls. The phase diagram of water shows that at 10 kPa the solid–liquid equilibrium line lies about 2 °C below the standard 0 °C freezing point at 1 atm. This is well above the triple‑point pressure (≈ 0.61 kPa), so ice can still coexist with liquid water, but the equilibrium temperature is lower.

So, if you cool liquid water down to about –2 °C while maintaining a pressure of 10 kPa, it will begin to freeze.
